statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. Let a be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] < pivot, let e be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = pivot, and let c be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > pivot. Let l_0 < l_1 < ... < l_{a-1} be the indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] < pivot, and let g_0 < g_1 < ... < g_{c-1} be the indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > pivot. Then len(r) = len(nums) = a + e + c, and for every t with 0 <= t < a, r[t] = nums[l_t], and for every t with 0 <= t < e, r[a + t] = pivot, and for every t with 0 <= t < c, r[a + e + t] = nums[g_t].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^6 <= nums[i] <= 10^6; and there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] = pivot.
